title: A candidate broken only by main's moves is sent back like a conflict, not counted as a rejection
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, `judge_pushed()`, `landing_candidate()`, `markers_note()`, `halt_reason()` and `HALT_AFTER`, `pushed_candidate()` and the module comment (step 4); `judge()` and `Verdict` in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs (how the gate is run: `<gate> <repo> <base> <candidate> <scenarios> [<scenario>]`, the verdict file, the wall clock); scripts/rsi/gate.sh (what it checks and in which order; `candidate does not build`, `candidate tests do not build`; you may not edit it); the `task.gated` case of `spawn_control_apply` (what each verdict does to the task and to `gate_rejections`/`gate_aborts`) and the verdicts `spawn_integrator_record` accepts, in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `DELIVERY_TASKS` (the `revise` step's record) and `OBJECTIVE_HISTORY` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs; `typed()` (a revision's text) in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs and `merge_main` in crates/spawn-cli/src/main_merge.rs (main is merged into a live worker's workspace when a task or revision is delivered); web/src/components/rsi/Verdicts.tsx and web/src/missionTimeline.ts; docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. A candidate that is right alone can be broken by what landed beside it, and today that counts against it as if it were wrong. On 2026-11-06 two tasks of mission 4 ran in parallel from the same main: task 36 added fields to `Facts`, and task 48 added a test that builds `Facts` without them. Task 36 landed first. Task 48's candidate, the merge of its pushed head with the new main, merged cleanly as text (different files), but did not compile: the gate said `candidate tests do not build`, the integrator recorded `rejected`, and the rejection counted toward the mission's three-in-a-row halt (`gate_rejections`), though neither task was wrong on its own base. Nothing in the record says that the head alone was fine, that the break came from main, or which of main's commits the worker must adapt to: its note is the gate's tail, and the worker reads it as its own mistake. A few such races in a busy mission halt it for no fault of any worker. A textual conflict is already handled this way: `conflict` sends the task back with main merged into its workspace and does not count. A semantic conflict needs the same treatment, decided by evidence, not by reading the gate's text.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. When it applies. The gate rejects a candidate C whose head does not contain main (`landing_candidate` built C as the merge of main and the pushed head, so C's tree is not the head's). Then, before recording any verdict, the integrator judges the head alone: the same gate (`SPAWN_GATE`, `gate::judge`), the same scenarios and task scenario, base = `git merge-base <head> <main>` (the main the head last took in; call it `head_base`), candidate = the pushed head itself. When the head contains main (C's tree is the head's), nothing changes: a rejection of C is a rejection. Never parse the gate's reason or output to decide this; the head's own verdict decides.
2. The verdicts.
- The head passes (the gate accepts it against `head_base`): the task is sent back with the new verdict `incompatible`. It moves the task to `revise` with the note, adds one to `revisions` like `rejected` and `conflict`, and leaves `gate_rejections` as it was (it is not a rejection of the work) and `gate_aborts` as `conflict` does. It is never a halt.
- The head fails too: `rejected`, counted, as today.
- The head's run gives no verdict (timeout, abort): record `aborted` as any gate abort is, naming the head; never `incompatible` on no evidence.
3. The record. The `task.gated` record of `incompatible` names, besides `base` (main), `revision` and `scenarios` as every verdict does: `candidate` (C, the merged commit the gate rejected), `head` (the pushed head, C's second parent), `head_base`, `head_verdict` (`accepted`), `main_commits` (main's first-parent commits in `head_base..base`, oldest first, full hashes: the commits the work must adapt to), `reason` (C's rejection reason), `log` (C's gate output) and `note`. A `rejected` record decided after a head run names `head`, `head_base` and `head_verdict` (`rejected`) as well, so the record shows why it counted.
4. The note sent back says what happened and what to do, from the record alone: that the work passes the gate on its own base but not merged with main; C's gate output (its tail, as `rejected` quotes it, so the compiler or test failure is there verbatim); each of `main_commits` by at least its 12-hex-digit prefix and its subject line (a landing's subject names its task and objective); and that main is merged into the workspace with this revision, so the work must be adapted to those commits. It is the `review_note` the dispatcher types (`typed()`), unchanged in how it is delivered.
5. The way back. Nothing new is needed: the dispatcher's delivery of the revision merges main into the idle workspace (`merge_main`), cleanly in this case, and says so in the text. The worker adapts, reports again, and the next pass judges it as any report.
6. Every reader of verdicts knows `incompatible`: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it; `spawn_control_apply` folds it as in 2; `DELIVERY_TASKS` takes it as the record a `revise` task is measured from (as `rejected` and `conflict`), so a stall of that step is measured from it (objective 013); the objective history and the RSI and Missions pages show it as its own verdict (a `revise`, not a rejection) in web/src (missions.ts, missionTimeline.ts, Verdicts.tsx, timelineStyle.ts as needed); the supervisor's digest, if it lists verdicts, names it.
7. Cost. The head's gate run happens only when C is rejected and C is a real merge; it doubles that pass's gate time and nothing else. Say so in the module comment.
8. Causality (§14): the decision rests on two recorded gate verdicts on named commits (C against main, the head against `head_base`), both in the record; nothing is inferred from timing or from the text of a reason.
State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (step 4, beside `conflict`), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 (the verdicts and the halt rule: what counts toward three in a row) and in docs/storage.md if it lists verdicts. Add unit tests in integrate.rs with a scratch mirror and a fake gate script, as the existing landing tests do:
- C rejected, the head accepted against its merge-base with main: `incompatible`, with `head`, `head_base`, `main_commits` and a note that quotes the gate's output and names the main commits;
- C rejected, the head rejected: `rejected`, naming the head's verdict;
- C rejected where the head contains main: `rejected`, with no second gate run;
- the head's run aborts: `aborted`;
- in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/, the fold: `incompatible` moves the task to `revise`, adds a revision, keeps `gate_rejections`; three `incompatible` in a row do not halt; `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/016.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge, no supervisor) runs three residents of one gated mission (accept = gate) on a fake engine; `spawn integrate --once` passes, run one at a time by the scenario, judge through a recording gate whose "build" stands for a struct and its initializers: every file under uses/ must name exactly the fields struct.txt names, or it rejects with `candidate tests do not build` and `error[E0063]: missing field ... in initializer of `Facts``. All three tasks are delivered from the same main and reported before the first pass. alpha adds field `c` (struct.txt and uses/ to `a b c`) and lands first. beta adds uses/beta.txt naming `a b`: right alone, broken merged (task 48's case). gamma adds uses/gamma.txt naming `a b z`: broken alone. Checked:
- (1) beta's first verdict after alpha's landing is `incompatible`, its pass leaves `gate_rejections` unchanged, beta is in `revise` and the mission is not halted;
- (2) the record: `base` is main, `candidate` the rejected merge (first parent main, second parent `head`), `head` on beta's pushed branch, `head_base` = merge-base(head, base), `head_verdict` `accepted`; the gate's own log shows it rejected (`base`, `candidate`) and accepted (`head_base`, `head`); `main_commits` holds alpha's landing (its `task.landed` `to`); the `note` holds the compiler line and alpha's landing commit (at least 7 hex digits);
- (3) the revision the dispatcher types into beta carries the compiler line and that commit;
- (4) gamma's verdict is `rejected`, its pass adds exactly one to `gate_rejections`, and the gate judged gamma's head alone too;
- (5) beta, sent back, gets main merged into its workspace with the revision, fixes uses/beta.txt to `a b c`, reports, and lands; the mission is not halted and main builds.
On the live main (115f078; the deployed binary is 3e2c08e) it fails at (1): "task #2, whose head passes the gate alone and fails only merged with main, was gated 'rejected' (candidate tests do not build), not 'incompatible'; gate_rejections 0 -> 1". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
